parts.text: Past experience has shown that the heights of a certain variety of plant have mean 64.0 cm and standard deviation 3.8 cm. During a particularly hot summer, it was expected that the heights of plants of this variety would be less than usual. In order to test whether this was the case, a botanist recorded the heights of a random sample of 100 plants and found that the value of the sample mean was 63.3 cm. Stating a necessary assumption, carry out the test at the 2.5% significance level.
